title: Rank-one recurrence, mass-degree drift and a recurrent higher-molecularity marked-method obstruction
status_authority: Supplied complete visible mathematics at its exact stated scope, with imported operations credited. No new independent Capital audit.
reported_status: The source recovers the known universal closed-class and rank-one recurrence arguments, derives a global mass-degree drift bound and strong restoring drift in a specified cone, and obtains nonexplosion when mass-changing linkage classes have maximum molecularity D<=2 even if mass-preserving classes have higher molecularity. Its reversible degree-five network has an exact recurrent product-Poisson law but defeats the direct fixed-residual terminal-rarity construction. Unrestricted weak-reversibility positive recurrence and the full high-molecularity/nonexplosion endpoint remain unresolved here; the method obstruction is not a recurrence counterexample.

Finite stochastic mass-action reaction graph with arbitrary finite species count, complexes in N_0^d, every constant rate kappa_r>0 and weak reversibility. Generator Lf(x)=sum_r kappa_r*(x)_(y_r)*(f(x+y'_r-y_r)-f(x)), with falling-factorial propensities and disabled sources. The full target quantifies over every initial population and every nonabsorbing reachable class: nonexplosion, positive recurrence, unique stationary probability and TV convergence. Absorbing singletons carry point mass. The full theorem assumes no complex balance, added outflows, given Lyapunov certificate, bounded class or stationary oracle. Rank-one, mass-degree and cone results retain their extra stated conditions.

proof_availability.classification_scope: Closed mutual reachability does not imply finite mean returns or nonexplosion. Rank-one ordering does not control competing directions in rank>=2. The degree-five example is explicitly positive recurrent and refutes only a direct terminal-rarity/fixed-residual proof extension; accepted binary one-linkage and earlier terminal-gap results remain at their original scopes.
